tagline.text: End your last day with a Manila Bay sunset and a Ferris wheel ride

location.label: Location
location.text: Bay City, Pasay, Metro Manila (Manila Bay reclamation area)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (sunsets are best in the November–May dry season)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–3,000 per person (excluding shopping and accommodation)

children.text: The largest shopping mall in the Philippines, standing on reclaimed land on Manila Bay. Sunsets from the waterfront promenade, the MOA Eye Ferris wheel, an ice rink and arena shows are all in one place, and its proximity to the airport makes it an especially good choice for your last day.
SM Mall of Asia (MOA for short) is the largest shopping mall in the Philippines, set at the tip of reclaimed land in Manila Bay, in Bay City, Pasay, Metro Manila. It opened on

, and with the Main Mall, the Entertainment Mall and the north and south parking buildings linked by walkways, its total floor area reaches about 500,000 m². With more than 600 shops and over 200 restaurants, a single loop around the mall can easily take up half a day.
But what makes MOA special for travelers is the sea rather than the shopping. Stand on SM by the Bay, the waterfront promenade that stretches about
1.5km
behind the mall, and you'll watch the sun go down across Manila Bay; as the

-tall MOA Eye Ferris wheel lights up, the amusement park and restaurant strip turn into a nighttime scene. Early each year an international fireworks competition is held just offshore, and on New Year's Eve hundreds of thousands of people gather here for the countdown.
The complex also brings together an indoor ice rink, the Mall of Asia Arena holding around 15,000 people, the MOA Sky rooftop park, a large IKEA store that opened in
, and the Museo del Galeón (Galleon Museum), which opened in
May 2026
. The Globe Rotunda, with its globe sculpture at the southern end of EDSA, is the gateway to MOA, and farther south lies Entertainment City, home to a cluster of casino resorts.
Best of all, it's just
15–40 minutes

by car from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), so it fits easily into a last-day plan. Many expats and travelers check out, store their luggage, enjoy some shopping, dinner and the sunset, then head off to catch a late-night flight. It suits families looking for a place to escape the heat and rain, travelers coming to see a show, and anyone who wants to spend an easy day in Manila.

blocks.title: Watch the sunset at SM by the Bay

children.text: From the waterfront promenade behind the mall, watch the sun set across Manila Bay. Sunset falls around
depending on the season; head out about 30 minutes early and claim a spot by the seawall to see the whole sky turn red. Admission is free.

blocks.title: Ride the MOA Eye Ferris wheel

children.text: This
-tall Ferris wheel with 36 air-conditioned gondolas has been running since
December 2011
. Fares are reportedly about
for a regular gondola and about
for a VIP gondola with a transparent floor; ride at dusk or after dark to take in both the sea and the city lights.

blocks.title: Amusement park and Seaside Boulevard stroll

children.text: Around the MOA Eye are about ten rides, including a carousel, a Viking ship, bumper cars and a drop tower. The ride area opens around
on weekdays and around
on weekends and runs until about midnight; entry is free, and you buy a ticket for each ride.
On the 3rd floor of the Main Mall is an Olympic-size ice rink of about 1,800 m². A 2-hour session costs about
on weekdays and about
on weekends and holidays, including skate and helmet rental. Entry is by time slot, so check availability at the on-site ticket counter or book online.

blocks.title: Shows at the Mall of Asia Arena

children.text: This indoor arena opened in
and seats about 15,000–16,000. It hosted the final phase of the FIBA Basketball World Cup in
and still regularly holds concerts and basketball and volleyball games. On event days the whole complex gets crowded, so check the schedule in advance.
About 60,000 m² of open space spreads across the Main Mall rooftop. There's a soccer field, a dog park, a prayer space, an outdoor amphitheater and a running track about
1km
long, and anyone can enter for free. The sunset from the sea-facing viewing deck is beautiful too.
The silver-domed building where Seaside Boulevard meets Sunset Avenue is the Museo del Galeón (Galleon Museum), which opened on
and displays a full-size galleon replica. Next to the arena is an IKEA store that opened in
November 2021
and is said to be the largest in the world.

The globe sculpture on the rotunda at the southern end of EDSA is the symbol of MOA. Inside the mall you can browse Philippine clothing brands, souvenirs such as dried mangoes and snacks, and a large supermarket all in one go, making it a great place to pick up gifts to take home.

items.title: Last-day route
items.subtitle: From checkout to a late-night flight

children.text: Check out of your hotel and take a Grab to MOA. Leave large luggage at your hotel or look into a luggage storage service in advance
Have lunch at the Main Mall restaurants and buy gifts to take home, such as dried mangoes and snacks, at the supermarket
Skate for
2 hours
at the ice rink or keep shopping in the cool indoors
Head out to SM by the Bay, stroll the waterfront promenade and claim a spot for the sunset
Watch the sunset over Manila Bay, then ride the MOA Eye after dark for the night views
Have dinner at the restaurants on Seaside Boulevard or inside the mall
For an international flight, book a Grab so you reach the airport
3 hours
before departure (usually
15–40 minutes
On Friday evenings, weekends and event days, traffic around MOA and on the way to the airport gets very heavy. On those days it's safer to leave for the airport an hour earlier.

items.title: Full-day route
items.subtitle: Museum in the morning, shopping in the afternoon, sunset in the evening

children.text: Arrive as the mall opens and look around the Globe Rotunda and the Main Mall
Visit the Museo del Galeón (check announcements for opening hours and fees)
Have lunch, then explore the IKEA store and the area around the arena to the north
Go up to the MOA Sky rooftop park and walk the sea-facing viewing deck and running track
Watch the sunset at SM by the Bay and try the rides
After dinner, head to Entertainment City to see the casino resorts lit up at night and their fountain shows
If you'd like to see more waterfront sunset spots, also check out the Roxas Boulevard promenade in the
Manila Bay
entry.
NAIA is about
5–8km
from MOA. By Grab it takes
15–20 minutes
without traffic and
40 minutes
or more at rush hour, and costs about
Since
September 28, 2026
, the base fare for ride-hailing cars such as Grab has gone up by
, and the airport taxi base fare is now
. Check the fare in the app or on the meter before you get in.
It takes about
20–40 minutes
from Makati and about
15–30 minutes
from Ermita or Malate in Manila. Choosing a precise drop-off point such as "Main Mall" or "SM by the Bay" cuts down on walking.
When leaving at night, the pickup area on the Seaside Boulevard side gets crowded, so booking from the Main Mall entrance or the north parking building often gets you a ride faster.
The EDSA Carousel bus, which runs in a dedicated lane down the middle of EDSA, stops at the "SM Mall of Asia" station. It runs
24 hours
a day from Monumento in the north to PITX in the south, so you can come from the Ayala area of Makati or from Ortigas without transferring.
Fares are distance-based:
for the first
5km
, then
per additional km (based on the September 28, 2026 fare increase). Cash is the most reliable option, and some buses also accept beep cards.
The nearest station is Redemptorist–Aseana station on LRT Line 1, about
2km
from MOA. If it's too hot to walk, call a Grab from the station.
From EDSA station on LRT Line 1 or Taft Avenue station on MRT Line 3, transfer to a jeepney or bus marked "MOA". The minimum jeepney fare is about
Within the complex, you get around on foot. It's about
5–10 minutes
from the Main Mall to SM by the Bay and about
10–15 minutes
to the arena and IKEA.
Buses bound for Cavite, Batangas and Laguna leave from the bus terminal south of MOA. Check routes and times on site.
Since MOA is mostly indoors, you can visit year-round, but for sunsets the clear-skied dry season of
November–May
is best.
December–February
in particular brings cool breezes that make the promenade pleasant to walk. In
March–May
daytime temperatures climb to around
, so it's best to stay inside the mall at midday and head out to the sea at dusk.
During the
June–October
rainy season, afternoon showers are frequent, and typhoons sometimes pass through in
July–October
. When a strong wind warning is issued, the MOA Eye and rides may stop and the promenade may be closed. Every year on Saturday nights in
February–March
, the Philippine International Pyromusical Competition is held just offshore (in
, from
February 21
to
March 21
), and huge crowds turn out for the fireworks and light displays during the Christmas season and on New Year's Eve.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Large hotels overlooking Manila Bay stand within and right next to the MOA complex; at hotels directly connected to SM by the Bay, such as Conrad Manila, sea-view rooms run about
a night. Business hotels across the road in Bay City cost about

and, being close to the airport, are handy for the night before an early-morning flight. The casino resorts of Entertainment City to the south let you enjoy casinos, shows and restaurants all in one place.

Food options are wide-ranging. The Main Mall has everything from Filipino fast food to Korean, Japanese and Chinese chains and food courts, while Seaside Boulevard is lined with sea-view buffet restaurants such as Vikings and La Fiesta. If you'd like to pick your own seafood, try the paluto style at Seaside Dampa on Macapagal Boulevard,
10–15 minutes
away by car: buy shrimp, crab and fish by weight, then have a neighboring restaurant cook it for you. Agree on the cooking fee before you buy.
From
, the mall is open daily
. Opening hours were cut back in
March–June 2026
due to a national energy emergency, so check SM announcements on holidays and during emergencies.
Head to the promenade 30 minutes before sunset to find a spot easily. The red sky that lingers for about 20 minutes after the sun goes down is the best time for photos.
Lines for the MOA Eye get long at dusk. Watch the sunset from the promenade first and ride after dark for a shorter wait and great night views.
The ice rink is cold even though it's inside the mall. Bring long sleeves and socks; you may have to buy gloves on site.
On arena event days, Grab fares go up and cars are hard to get. It's easier to check the event schedule in advance and pick another day.
On your last day, confirm your departure terminal in advance. NAIA Terminals 1, 2 and 3 serve different airlines, and moving between terminals takes time too.
The air conditioning inside the mall is strong, so you'll get cold if you stay long. Even if it's hot outside, bring a light layer.
Gifts to take home are often cheaper at the mall's large supermarket than at the airport. Pack liquids and sauces in your checked baggage.
The trip to the airport on your last day can take longer than you expect. During rush hour (
), on Friday evenings and on rainy days, even a
5–8km
ride can take close to an hour, so for international flights aim to arrive 3 hours before departure and leave with plenty of time to spare.
On fireworks competition nights, New Year's Eve and big concert days, crowds are huge and pickpocketing can occur. Keep your phone and wallet in a bag worn in front.
Do not climb down onto the seawall rocks or go beyond the railings. At high tide and on days with big waves, the edge of the promenade gets wet and slippery.
Manila Bay is not for swimming. Do not go into the water off the promenade.
Bags are checked at the mall and arena entrances. Do not bring items such as knives or sprays.
Rides stop in strong winds or rain and sometimes close for maintenance. Check the latest notices at the on-site ticket booth for operating status and fares.
